contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, DAG, the envelope schema
Records: envelope, append-only table, entities, idempotency, compare-and-swap, migrations, stream, apply
Leases: table, fencing, heartbeats, attempts, slots
Tickets: tickets, claims, file claims, ticket sets, id mint
Service tables: forge, backups, ticks, health, code table, registry, plans

pointers.shared: The envelope as JSON Schema 2020-12; every node schema should $ref it
N-01 owns the store, the migrations of the core tables and the id form
N-02 owns leases, the fencing token counter and heartbeats
N-45 owns retention and the cleanup registry

purpose.s: One store, no broker (principles.xml#one-store): SQLite in WAL mode at STATE/store/coq.db, opened by the Go service alone, served over one gRPC unix socket; every record of every node is a row here and nothing lives on a branch, in a file tree or in a second database.
The node that owns a table owns its forward-only migration; a node that needs a column on another node's table cuts a ticket against that node's volume.
This volume names the tables and rules; the owning node volume carries the mechanism and the schema beside it.

store-rule.title: The record envelope every kind carries
store-rule.statement: Fields: id (string, form YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-CODE-xxxxx: UTC stamp, the code, five lowercase alphanumerics; unique per writer), at (UTC 2006-01-02T15:04:05Z, assigned by N-01 at commit when absent), kind (dotted lowercase), code (an integer in the live code table), node (N-xx that wrote it), by (node id or seat id, optional), attempt (0..3 where one applies; 0 means none), key (idempotency key, optional), version (expected version for a compare-and-swap put, optional), seq (assigned by N-01, never on input), lease_token (fencing token, required on every system-job write), ticket (optional), note (max 240), hash (canonical JSON by RFC 8785 of the body, set by N-01).

Ruling on the id form: N-01 owns the records table and today's event writers already mint the UTC-stamp form (events/schema/event.schema.json), so the book keeps it; the r-prefixed form some G4 and G7 schemas repeat is rejected with reason (rejected-with-reason.xml#envelope-id-form) and those schemas $ref state-store.schema.json#/$defs/envelope by their own ticket.
store-rule.source: N-01 spec.xml#input; events/schema/event.schema.json; G5 schemas embed it by allOf; N-43 record.schema.json#/$defs/envelope.

store-table.name: records
store-table.purpose: Every record of every kind; the only log; seq strictly increasing; a row is never updated or deleted except by N-45 retention.
store-table.rule: Indexes: (kind, seq), (ticket, seq), (code, seq); the query "newest record of kind K for key X with code C" is one index read.
A put whose code is not in the live code table is 400 with the live hash in the reason; a put of a line-op kind by a seat is 403; a duplicate id is 409 record.conflict key=id.
A multi-record put under one idempotency key commits all rows or none (N-51 verdict plus freeze flip).

store-table.name: entities
store-table.purpose: Current state by key (ticket entities, flags, counters, snapshots, health); every write is compare-and-swap on version and is also a record.
store-table.rule: version grows by one per write; updated_seq is the seq of the record that last wrote it; expected 0 inserts.

store-table.name: idempotency
store-table.purpose: A seen key replays its response with code 200; the same key with a different payload is 409 record.conflict; the same payload is a no-op.
store-table.rule: Keys in use: pr:head:verdict, pr:head, pr:head:conflict, main_sha:hold, hold:ID:aged, lease_key:generation, node:N-xx:KEY for every system job, sha plus attempt (N-35), atlas sha256 (N-36), client id plus counter (N-38, N-39, N-41, N-42), window plus tick minute (N-40), card source id (N-28), message id (N-30), set_id plus key (N-18).

store-rule.title: Idempotent puts
store-rule.statement: Every automated step writes under a key; a retry of the step replays the first response (200) and never creates a second record; a step whose outcome is unknown re-runs by its key (failure-cases.xml#unknown-outcome).

store-rule.title: Compare-and-swap
store-rule.statement: An entity write carries expected_version; a miss is 409 with the current version in the reason and the writer re-reads; expected 0 inserts; used by lease generation, merge.hold.lifted, forge:snapshot, backup:latest, tick:*, health:service, flag:hold, build-mode.state, break-glass.token, alert.ack, the tier pointer, page.state, ack, plan.step and plan.side.

store-rule.title: Forward-only migrations
store-rule.statement: Table migrations(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name, node, applied_at); applied in order at open inside one transaction each; never a down migration; the node owning a table owns its migration file under scheduler/internal/store/migrations/ and its test; a migration that fails leaves the store closed (store.corrupt 500) rather than half-applied.

store-rule.title: The record.committed stream
store-rule.statement: Subscribe(class, filter, Last-Event-ID) streams seq in order over gRPC; a client that reconnects sends its last seq and re-reads the full snapshot of its class before applying new frames (D21, principles.xml#level-triggered); a slow client past stream.buffer is dropped (429 push.client.dropped) and re-subscribes; nothing is lost because the log is the truth.

store-rule.title: Apply rules by kind
store-rule.statement: Compare-and-swap upsert by version for page.state, ack, plan.step and plan.side; append-only for ledger.row, reply and owner.message; every apply is also a record so the stream carries it.

store-rule.title: The code table
store-rule.statement: Table code_table(hash UNIQUE, main_sha, loaded_at, version, body JSON): the status code map loaded by N-43 from shared/status-codes.xml at the merge sha; N-01 reads the newest row to validate every put; a failed load keeps the previous row and writes code.table 400 with the live hash.

store-table.name: leases
store-table.purpose: One holder per key; the fencing token orders writers; generation bumps on every grant and expiry.
store-table.column: ticket:phase:attempt for seats (CR-<request id>:spec:attempt for a cut request); node:N-xx:KEY for system jobs, including node:N-07:leader (the scheduler leader, ttl lease.leader_ttl_seconds 30, renewed every 10 s); merge.lock; watcher/<page>; cleanup:ENTRY, workspace:TICKET, seat:RUN, tier:NAME, backup:SNAPSHOT, publish:drive, unlanded:run, cutover:run, exittest:DAY
store-table.rule: The token counter is entity counter:lease_token and only grows; the merge.lock lease is 120 s; the default system-job ttl is PT15M; a renew is accepted only for the current generation.
A script may ask whether a path is held (lease list --path) before it deletes anything (N-45).

store-rule.title: Fencing tokens
store-rule.statement: The store-wide fencing token only grows; N-01 refuses a put whose token is not current for the record's ticket and attempt (412 record.stale) and logs it; N-39 shows the token beside the last records; a stale writer learns it lost and exits.

store-table.name: heartbeats
store-table.purpose: Latest heartbeat per run (upsert with monotonic seq); N-12 reads it for the stall bound; N-39 shows the age.
store-table.rule: An older generation on a heartbeat is 412; adopted is true after a launcher restart re-entered the beat loop.

store-table.name: attempts
store-table.purpose: One row per attempt of a ticket phase with its backoff and outcome; dead after 3.
store-table.rule: Unique on (ticket, phase, n); backoff min(10 s x 2^(n-1), 300 s); row 4 never exists.

store-table.name: slots
store-table.purpose: Workspace slots 1..workspace_slots; compare-and-swap from null to holder; reclaimed by expiry plus seat.result.

store-table.name: tickets
store-table.purpose: The whole ticket as a record; status is the closed set cut, waiting, ready, in_flight, done, dead, cancelled, refused.
store-table.column: set by N-03 when it admits the ticket set cut from N-10's fix-for-hold ticket.request (rejected_id plus hold_id); N-09 reads it for the hold exception; a second fix ticket naming a hold is refused until the first is verified or dead
with source_sha when files come from feat/go-scheduler-design-one-xml-spec-per-domain-unde (small cut)
store-table.rule: Transitions: cut to waiting or ready or refused; waiting to ready or cancelled or dead (stale); ready to in_flight; in_flight to done or ready (next attempt) or dead or cancelled; any other is 409 ticket.transition_refused. cancelled carries reason and ruling id.
Queries: by status at a sha; children of an epic by status; by kind and by over an at range.

store-table.name: claims
store-table.purpose: The proof of one file, one in-flight ticket: taken in the ticket.ready transaction, released in the terminal transaction.

store-table.name: file_claims
store-table.purpose: Claims by pattern and prefix at workspace start (N-14), unique on prefix for in-flight tickets; released by N-45 on merge, dead or cancel.
store-table.rule: A second in-flight ticket on tools/map/registry/** or on one screen volume is refused (N-37).

store-table.name: ticket_sets
store-table.purpose: ticket-set.draft and ticket-set.accepted by set_id with anchor, repo_sha, attempt and verdict_ref.

store-table.name: id_mint
store-table.purpose: Reserved ticket ids, unique on (set_id, key) and on id, so a crashed mint resumes with the same ids.

store-table.name: flags
store-table.purpose: The three flags: build-mode, hold, freeze; each with state, scope, expiry, the card and ruling that set it.

store-rule.title: The hold flag
store-rule.statement: Entity flag:hold (a row of flags) is set and cleared by N-29 from a ruling or a Controls action by compare-and-swap; N-03, N-07 and N-09 read it at the start of every tick before any dispatch or merge; ticks, health, backups, the poll and the push transport never stop under hold; a dispatch under a set flag writes 500 hold.ignored (N-42).

store-rule.title: Build mode state
store-rule.statement: Entity build-mode.state (flags row build-mode): state on or off, scope, expires_at, ruling_id, version; written by N-44, read by N-07 at dispatch and copied into the dispatch record with its version; cleared by the system at expiry (max flags.build_mode.max_duration P7D) with one card when rebuild tickets are still open.

store-table.name: forge_history
store-table.purpose: Entity forge:snapshot (main_sha, previous_main_sha, changed_paths, main_gate, prs[] with head sha, head repository, base ref, mergeability, changed files and the coq/gate status: state, description, target_url, updated_at; hash, polled_at, stale, failed_since, etags) is written every poll by compare-and-swap; this table is appended on hash change.
store-table.retention: forge.keep_days 30; cleanup-forge.sh; the live entity is never touched.

store-table.name: backups
store-table.purpose: One row per snapshot; entities backup:latest (compare-and-swap) and backup:running (expected absent).
store-table.retention: cleanup.backup_keep daily 14, weekly 8, monthly 6; the newest verified backup is never deleted.

store-rule.title: Ticks
store-rule.statement: Entities tick:SUBKIND (n, at, interval_seconds, class for backup) written by compare-and-swap once per tick (scheduler, poll, backup, stall, health, hourly, daily); the tick record carries subkind, n, at and duration_ms; the tick minute keys a counters window; a skipped tick is tick.missed once per subkind and counters.failed for the stats screen.

store-rule.title: Health
store-rule.statement: Entity health:service (status, reasons[], counters, version, config_hash, at; includes the Jenkins GET /api/json probe with a 10 s timeout, unknown when missing) and table health_history(at, status, reasons JSON) appended on transition; pruned by cleanup-logs.sh --health.

store-rule.title: The record kinds registry
store-rule.statement: Every record kind with its code set, class (record, line-op, owner-surface, plan, screen), writer node and schema path; loaded by N-43 with the code table; a put of an unregistered kind is 400 and a kind under a code not listed for it is 400.

The registry is generated: shared/record-kinds.xml, written by rebuild/design/bin/make-kinds.py from the status-codes section of every node volume, so the node that emits a kind is the only place it is declared (check.sh C15 refuses a stale file; C18 refuses a kind whose code row in status-codes.xml does not name it). What broke (gap review R-03, 2026-10-14): the hand list that stood here by group omitted most kinds the volumes emit (every store.* kind, dispatch.refused, seat.bundle.refused, every deploy.* and art.* kind, push.failed and more), so N-01 would have refused the factory's own records. test.proof is emitted by N-24 for dark builds (nodes/N-24/spec.xml#m-mirror).

Not record kinds: views (map.state, node.state, checklist.state, alert, health, hold.flag, counters and the others of nodes/N-31/spec.xml#views) are derived by the service and pushed by subscription; static kinds (node.spec, source.inventory, nodes/N-37/spec.xml#static-kinds) are generated into the map bundle at build. A panel binds one of the three (check.sh C20).

Line-op class (refused 403 from a seat): code.table, build-mode.state, rule.bit, cleanup.run, disposition, cancel, pr.close, branch.delete, promotion, exit.verdict, freeze.state, merge, verified, dispatch, job.run, ticket.request, lease.*, any flag. bin/make-kinds.py reads this statement for the class column, so this sentence is the one list.

store-table.name: plans
store-table.purpose: Suite and main plans with their Jenkins build numbers so a restart re-attaches to a running build; in-flight caps live in config (gate runs 2 with main first, image builds 2).

store-table.name: suite_budget
store-table.purpose: Per suite: p95 of pod.run durations x 1.5, floor 5 min, cap 30 min, needs 20 samples; computed nightly.

store-rule.title: Owner-surface tables (G5)
store-rule.statement: cards(id, tier, source_record, dedupe_key, about, decide, options JSON, recommendation, default, deadline_at, status, version); rulings(card_id UNIQUE, pick, words, source, signal, at); messages(id, text, reply_to, at); acks(message_id, state, at, version); replies(message_id, text, at); routed_messages(message_id, lane, consumer, sla_seconds, at); watcher_alive(tier PRIMARY KEY, pid, heartbeat_at, version: the lock with heartbeat per tier); page_state(tier, version, rendered_seq, staleness, at); front_door(tier, bind, port, pid, at); plan_steps(plan_id, n, status, version); plan_sides(plan_id, n, status, version); ledger_rows(plan_id, seq, status, code, text, at); push_receipts(card_id, channel, delivered_at); cutover(page, state, imported_at, swapped_at, version).

store-rule.title: Governance tables (G7)
store-rule.statement: cleanup_runs(id, entry, plan_path, state, attempt, deleted JSON, remaining JSON, at); dispositions(entry_id, section, key, verdict, action, step, state, attempt, result_ref); publish_cursor(last_published_sha, version, at); promotions(tier, sha, attempt, state, pid, port, screenshot_id, previous_sha); exit_verdicts(day PRIMARY KEY, code, rows JSON, consecutive_fails); build_mode is the flags row.

store-rule.title: Map registries (G6)
store-rule.statement: bindings and machines are generated files in the repository (tools/map/registry/, N-37), not tables; their binding.record and binding.check rows are records; alerts are entities keyed by source record id with an alert.ack entity per acknowledgement.

store-table.name: counters
store-table.purpose: The counters view the Go service computes every tick for windows 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 d and the previous window of each, keyed by window plus tick minute; single writer; a lower-at frame is dropped; never a second metrics database.
store-table.rule: Every count is a count over record kinds in records, never a seat tally.

retention.s: Retention is a class per kind registered with N-45: record (records kept for the life of the store; the daily backup is the archive), owner-surface (page.state 7 days, other page.* 90 days, messages and replies for the life of the store), plan (90 days), screen (pushed frames not stored, frame.report 7 days), lease (released or expired rows 30 days), forge (forge_history 30 days), health (health_history 30 days), heartbeat (7 days after seat.result).

Every state path under the store's root (STATE/store/coq.db, its WAL, STATE/backups/, STATE/run/service.lock, STATE/config/service.env) is an entry in shared/cleanup-registry.json with line/bin/cleanup.sh --entry ID as its verb; the live database file is never a cleanup target.

Free space: a put is refused 503 store.disk under store.min_free_mib and a backup is skipped once under backup.min_free_mib; N-45 cleanup runs first and one card follows if still under (failure-cases.xml#disk-full).

config-keys.s: Keys live in STATE/config/service.env (the read token as COQ_FORGE_READ_TOKEN) and the config table; Scheduler.Reload applies a change without a restart; every value is a key, never a literal in code (K10).
config-keys.config-key: one key read by N-02, N-07, N-12 and N-15; N-12's dead-launcher bound is 3 x this (90 s)

config-key.name: executor.verbs
config-key.default: cleanup plan PT2M apply PT10M; publish-drive PT10M; promote PT5M; screenshot PT90S; unlanded plan PT5M apply PT1H per step

config-keys.config-key: scheduler.proto Executor.Run verb table

many-agents.readers: Every node reads through N-01's gRPC API; fifty readers at once are one SQLite WAL reader each; the stream fans out seq in order to every subscriber.
many-agents.writers: One process (the Go service) holds the write lock; every write is a transaction with compare-and-swap on version or an idempotency key; a seat never holds the file; a second service instance is refused by flock on STATE/run/service.lock (failure-cases.xml#duplicate-instance).
many-agents.collision: Two writers on one entity: the second compare-and-swap misses and gets 409 with the current version; two writers on one lease key: the second gets lease.refused 423; two puts with one key: the second replays 200 or, with a different payload, 409; a writer with a stale fencing token: 412; none of these waits and none overwrites.
many-agents.test: N-01 test: 20 goroutines put under one idempotency key; exactly one row; 19 replays. N-02 test: 20 claims on one key; one holder; 19 refusals naming it.
